title: Migrating to Java switch expressions
summary: After Java 11 was dropped, Peter (pvary) asked how to adopt the new switch syntax, given that Manu Zhang's PR #15176 migrates all switch statements at once and disrupts large in-flight PRs and internal forks. He listed three options: one large PR now, merging it shortly before a release, or migrating incrementally in new or touched code; he preferred the first or second. Maximilian Michels and Manu favoured merging before the release. In June Neelesh Salian revived the thread for 1.12, scoping the work to switches and pattern-matching instanceof in iceberg-core based on #15494. Eduard Tudenhöfner and Kevin Liu asked for the instanceof changes in a separate PR. The core switch change merged as #16881, but concerns about switching in large chunks were raised at the community sync on June 24th; Neelesh reported the decision to revert the core changes for now, with similar future changes in individual PRs at the reviewer's discretion. Eduard linked the revert PR #16953.

positions.stance: Prefers one large migration PR, either now or shortly before the release, over incremental adoption.
Favours using Java 17 language features and merging the migration shortly before the release, noting that Flink 1.20 lacks proper Java 17 support.
Merging shortly before the release works for most people, and IDE support makes it easy to reapply the changes.
Do a scoped change for 1.12 covering switches and pattern-matching instanceof in iceberg-core only.
In favour of switch expressions for readability, but the instanceof changes should be a separate PR.

outcome.note: The core switch-expression change (#16881) was merged, then concerns were raised at the community sync; Neelesh Salian reported the decision to revert the core changes for now (revert PR #16953), with similar changes going forward in individual PRs at the reviewer's discretion.

why_it_matters: Bulk syntax-modernization PRs are not being accepted for now; contributors should keep such changes small and expect them to be at the reviewer's discretion.
